description: Labelled ground-truth corpus for PER-05/06/07/08 — perimeter-access-audit's second half, added after PER-01/02/03/04 were frozen. Kept separate from cases.json (PER-01/02/04) rather than merged into it, since that corpus's fixtures were never designed to also carry llms-full.txt/sitemap.xml/.md inputs.

cases.note: No sitemap exists at all — PER-06 correctly fires (a real defect); PER-08 must NOT also fire for the same root cause, since 'not referenced in robots' is meaningless once there is nothing to reference. Exactly one finding, not two, proves PER-08's applicability guard.

cases.label: clean
cases.note: Wildcard-only robots.txt (no named AI groups), a sitemap that agrees with a clean, non-noindexed page, and no TDM reservation anywhere. C5 must also stay silent here since robots.txt never named an AI agent — the precision guard.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: Every AI agent is blocked at the root — PER-02 correctly fires (a real defect). PER-09's C1 must NOT also fire for the sitemap-declared URLs under the same root cause: a root-wide block is PER-01/02's finding, not a new path-specific PER-09 contradiction (the absence of a C1 finding here proves the overlap-control guard at the corpus level, not just in isolated unit tests). C5 is orthogonal and legitimately still fires: the site named specific AI agents (even to block them), which is exactly the demonstrated-engagement precision guard C5 requires, and no TDM declaration exists.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: GPTBot may fetch the root but is disallowed from /pricing specifically, and the sitemap declares /pricing as canonical. C5 also fires here since named AI groups exist and no TDM declaration is published — two distinct, legitimate PER-09 findings from one fixture.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: /pricing is declared canonical in sitemap.xml but its response carries X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: tdmrep.json reserves TDM rights, but robots.txt still allows GPTBot/ClaudeBot/CCBot to crawl the root. C5 stays silent here since tdmrep.json IS present. sitemap_status is absent, so PER-06 legitimately also fires (a real, separate defect) — included in expected_findings rather than isolated by a fixture that would obscure how PER-09 composes alongside an unrelated PER-06 finding.

cases.label: defect
cases.note: The root page's X-Robots-Tag header says noindex while its own <meta name="robots"> tag says index, follow. sitemap_status is absent, so PER-06 legitimately also fires alongside PER-09's own finding.
